study_families.study_label: Secondary analysis of control (placebo) arms of two bovine-colostrum RCTs (acute and 4-week supplementation trials), re-analysed for plasma vitamin D status effects on innate immune and metabolomic responses to a single acute prolonged cycling bout
study_families.design: Secondary/observational re-analysis; single-arm (placebo/control-arm participants only, pooled from two parent RCTs) acute-exercise study with a single identifiable bout (2.5 h cycling at 15%Delta, ~55-60% VO2max); participants stratified post hoc into deficient (plasma 25(OH)D <33 nmol/L, n=7) vs non-deficient (>33 nmol/L, n=16) groups. No vitamin D supplementation was given to this sample -- vitamin D status is an endogenous/observational classifier, not an intervention.
registry_ids: NR (parent RCTs registered per ref. 26, Davison et al. 2020 SMS 25(6):788-796, which is not one of the 10 pilot reports and was not separately retrieved)
study_families.training_load: NA (acute single-bout study; no multi-week training programme)
study_families.cointerventions: None in the analysed sample: 'The participants in this study took part in the control (placebo) arm of these trials' (p.2, Methods, Design) -- i.e. the bovine-colostrum supplement itself is explicitly excluded from this analysis, so no supplement co-intervention confounds the exercise effect here (FT08 separability: satisfied, because only the non-supplemented control arm is used).
study_families.study_notes: Participants were drawn from the control/placebo arms of two separate parent colostrum RCTs (an acute trial and a 4-week trial per ref. 26) and pooled into one n=23 secondary-analysis sample; this pooling of two parent-trial control arms into one cohort for this report is noted here but not independently verified against ref. 26.

reports.title: Vitamin D status modulates innate immune responses and metabolomic profiles following acute prolonged cycling
reports.authors: Jones AW; Mironas A; Mur LAJ; Beckmann M; Thatcher R; Davison G
reports.reviewer_notes: Provisional view only (extraction pilot, not a screening decision): single identifiable acute bout (2.5h cycling), pre-exercise baseline, >=1 post-cessation immune-related sample (post-exercise and 1h post-exercise), adults, generally healthy -- fits A_core_acute cleanly. No supplement confound in this subset (placebo/control arm only), so FT08 (supplement/feeding co-intervention not separable) does NOT apply here.
reports.author_stated_use: Authors frame the work as identifying vitamin D status as a determinant of innate-immune (neutrophil) and metabolomic responses to acute strenuous endurance exercise, supporting monitoring of circulating 25(OH)D and considering vitamin D3 supplementation strategies in athletic populations (p.2987-2988, Discussion/Conclusion); they explicitly do NOT aim to define optimal 25(OH)D thresholds in this study (p.2987).
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2977 Introduction: "transient perturbations of cellular and mucosal immunity occurring following prolonged, strenuous exercise (commonly referred to as an 'open window' of immunodepression)"

p.2986 Discussion: "Blunted blood neutrophil responses to in vitro stimuli are one of the classical measures of the 'open window' period of immune dysfunction following acute prolonged endurance exercise"

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Standard automated haematology analyser (Pentra 60 C+); no in-study CV/ICC reported for leukocyte counts. Granularity note: scored at marker_family level (not per individual analyte) for pilot practicality; see unresolved_questions.

Explicit single-bout timing: pre-exercise, immediate post-exercise ('within a few min of exercise cessation'), and 1 h post-exercise, all within the 0-72h organising window (0_to_lt30min and 30min_to_lt3h bins).
Total/differential leukocyte counts and neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio are direct, immune-specific cellular measures.
Within-subject repeated measures across 3 timepoints with group-level SD reported (n=7/16), but no ICC/CV or responder-threshold analysis for individual leukocyte trajectories.

Leukocyte/lymphocyte counts and neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio are co-measured alongside neutrophil function and metabolomics but no explicit within-study association test links them to a functional or clinical endpoint; no infection follow-up was conducted.
Established clinical assay; not a novel candidate requiring validation in this study.
Routine venous blood draw and automated haematology counting; standard clinical feasibility, implicit in Methods rather than explicitly discussed.

source_locator: p.2979-2980 Methods, In vitro blood neutrophil function
precision_validation.evidence_notes: PMA-stimulated chemiluminescence run in duplicate per sample with the unstimulated area subtracted; both assays reference prior validated methods ([27,31-34] in the source paper).
Same explicit single-bout timing as the leukocyte family (pre/post/1h, within the 0-72h window); neutrophil function assays performed on blood held <=2h at room temperature before testing.
Direct ex vivo functional assays on neutrophils (degranulation/elastase release in response to bacterial extracts; oxidative burst in response to PMA) -- immune-specific by design.

Individual-level change expressed as % of own pre-exercise value (within-subject normalisation) and a positive correlation between plasma 25(OH)D and the magnitude of change (r=0.458, p=0.028) is reported, which is some individual-level signal, but no formal ICC/CV/responder classification is given.

These ARE direct ex vivo functional assays (not just co-measured counts): bacterial-stimulated elastase release and PMA-stimulated oxidative burst are genuine immune-effector-function tests, and a within-cohort association between plasma 25(OH)D and change in bacterial-stimulated elastase is reported (r=0.458, p=0.028). No clinical/infection endpoint was tracked (clinical_endpoint=none_reported).

No independent-cohort or external validation of the vitamin-D-by-neutrophil-function association; authors explicitly call for 'a larger, and appropriately powered, sample...to fully investigate the effects of a wide range of circulating 25(OH)D thresholds' and a study design 'that would allow cause and effect to be established' (p.2987) -- i.e. they themselves flag this as not yet validated.

Ex vivo assays on fresh whole blood within 2h of draw; feasible in a research lab setting but requires same-day processing (less field-feasible than a simple blood count), not explicitly discussed as a feasibility limitation by the authors.

Targeted linoleic/arachidonic-acid quantification used standard curves; untargeted FIE-MS identifications were confirmed by high-resolution FT-ICR-MS (1 ppm mass accuracy); FDR correction applied to the group x time ANOVA. No participant-level technical-replicate CV reported. Granularity note: scored at marker_family level (not per individual analyte) for pilot practicality; see unresolved_questions.
Same explicit pre/post/1h single-bout timing as other families, within the 0-72h organising window.

The 8 discriminatory metabolites (purine/pyrimidine catabolites, linoleic acid, tyrosine/adrenaline, lactate) are general metabolic-stress/inflammation-pathway markers, not immune-cell-specific; authors frame them as reflecting 'a greater physical stress response' rather than a specific immune mechanism, and link to immunity only via the linoleic-acid/arachidonic-acid/eicosanoid pathway narrative, not a direct immune assay.

Group-level (deficient vs non-deficient) differences are reported via multivariate PCA/ANOVA; no individual-level reliability, variance decomposition or responder analysis for metabolite trajectories is reported.

Metabolomic changes are co-measured with the neutrophil-function and leukocyte findings and discussed narratively (e.g. vitamin D status 'may be a contributing factor in the immune responses'), but no formal statistical association test links specific metabolites to the immune-function measures in this paper; no clinical/infection endpoint was tracked.

Exploratory/discovery-only metabolomic profiling in n=23 (7 vs 16); no independent-cohort replication; authors note the lack of statistical power and call for 'a larger, and appropriately powered, sample.'
Untargeted/targeted MS metabolomics requires specialised instrumentation (LTQ, FT-ICR-MS); authors do not explicitly discuss field feasibility of these assays for routine athlete monitoring.

Standard ELISA kits used per manufacturer instructions; blood-contamination screening (salivary transferrin >1 mg/dL exclusion) is itself a data-quality/reliability safeguard, but no CV/ICC is reported for the sLac/sLys assays themselves. Granularity note: scored at marker_family level (not per individual analyte) for pilot practicality; see unresolved_questions.
Same explicit pre/post/1h single-bout timing as other families, within the 0-72h organising window.

Salivary lactoferrin and lysozyme are recognised mucosal antimicrobial/innate-immune effector proteins; immune-specific by design, though the marker_family controlled vocabulary has no dedicated category for AMPs distinct from mucosal_sIgA (coded here as 'other'; see unresolved_questions).
No ICC/CV or individual-level reliability reported; sample attrition (blood contamination, n reduced to 5/10) further limits what can be said about individual variability.

No significant main effect of vitamin D group (or group x time interaction) was found for any sLac/sLys metric (concentration, secretion rate, or osmolality ratio); the domain was examined but the vitamin-D/AMP relationship was null in this study. No clinical/infection endpoint was tracked; authors attribute the null result partly to reduced n from blood-contamination exclusions.
No candidate validation attempted for these established mucosal markers in this study (null result reported, not a validation test).

Saliva is a non-invasive matrix, but this study's own data illustrate a feasibility limitation: 8/23 participants' saliva samples were excluded for blood contamination, reducing usable n by ~35% (23->15 pooled across groups).

eligibility_opinion.rationale: A single identifiable acute bout (2.5 h cycling at 15%Delta, ~55-60% VO2max) with an explicit pre-exercise baseline and two post-cessation sample timepoints (immediate post-exercise and 1 h post-exercise), in generally healthy, recreationally active adult males (p.2978-2979, Methods). The analysed sample is restricted to the control/placebo arm of two colostrum RCTs -- 'participants in this study took part in the control (placebo) arm of these trials' (p.2, Design) -- so the supplement/feeding co-intervention is fully separable and does not confound the exercise effect (FT08 not triggered); the deficient/non-deficient vitamin-D split is a post-hoc observational stratification of this single cohort, not a second exercise arm.

unresolved_questions: marker_family vocabulary gap: salivary antimicrobial peptides (lactoferrin/lysozyme) do not fit any existing marker_family value (not mucosal_sIgA, not cytokine_or_inflammatory_mediator, not immunoglobulin_or_complement); coded here as 'other' with a note -- consider whether the controlled list needs a dedicated 'mucosal_innate_AMP' or similarly named value, since AMPs are a recognised exercise-immunology marker class distinct from sIgA.

Study-family pooling: this report's n=23 sample is a secondary analysis pooling control-arm participants from two separate parent RCTs (an acute trial and a 4-week trial, per ref. 26 Davison et al. 2020) that are not among the 10 pilot reports and were not independently retrieved/verified here; guidance is needed on whether study_families/cohorts should flag or split by parent-trial origin when a report itself does not break out n per parent trial.

Vitamin-D-status subgroups (deficient/non-deficient) were treated as sample_set-level strata within one cohort rather than as two separate cohort rows, since they are a post-hoc biomarker split of a single recruited/randomised sample rather than two separately recruited populations; confirm this matches the intended cohort-vs-stratum convention, especially since Table 1 reports group-specific baseline characteristics.

Targeted linoleic-acid and arachidonic-acid values (Fig. 4A-B) are only available as a line graph with no table of exact numbers; effect_value for M-R12-027/028 is qualitative (direction/pattern only) and effect_value_source is 'reported_main_text_or_table' rather than a predeclared digitized_from_figure extraction, since no numeric digitization was performed in this pass -- flag whether these two rows should instead go through the formal two-reviewer figure-digitization protocol (manual section on effect/individual reproducibility) rather than being left qualitative.

Granularity of precision_validation: scored at marker_family level (leukocyte_redistribution, neutrophil_function, metabolome_or_lipidome, 'other'/saliva AMP) rather than per individual named analyte (e.g. bacterial-stimulated elastase scored separately from PMA-CL within neutrophil_function); flagged as a tractability choice, consistent with the same granularity question raised for R42.

Untargeted metabolomics tested_universe_n is NR because the paper never states the total number of m/z features screened (only the 8 top discriminatory metabolites surviving FDR-corrected ANOVA are named in Table 3); guidance is needed on whether 'NR' is correct here or whether the four scan ranges / acquisition parameters (Methods, Plasma metabolomics) should be used to estimate an approximate tested-universe size.
